1. The Problem

At peak times nobody can count on a mall parking bay, so shoppers circle or go elsewhere, and malls lose the visit

Saturday, 7:30 pm filmA family with cinema tickets, a pram and a grandparent heads to KL East Mall. Will there be a bay near the lifts at 7 pm? Today, nobody can promise one.

Finding a bay is a gamble

~25 min
a day KL drivers spend looking for parking. Search time rises steeply as a car park fills.

So shoppers go elsewhere

40%
of drivers have avoided shops because of parking; 26% gave up a trip.

Nobody can guarantee a bay

67%
of drivers would pay to reserve a space. Even SDP's KL East Mall tells event visitors to take the LRT "if mall parking is full".

Who is affected

Shoppers lose time, hardest for families, older shoppers and cinema-goers. Loyal shoppers, a mall's best customers, get no help finding a bay. Malls lose visits to easier rivals.

Why it matters to SDP

SDP's four township malls each draw hundreds of thousands to over a million visitors. Recurring income is ~10% of SDP's total against a 30% goal, and parking is every visitor's first experience.

Sources: BCG "Unlocking Cities" 2018 (via World of Buzz); Müller et al. 2026; INRIX 2017 (UK, US); ParkMobile 2024; YSDAF KL East Mall guide; SDP. No simulated figures on this slide.

2. Target User

Three groups lose out today: SDP's malls, their most loyal shoppers, and everyone else who drives in

Who the family isRegular KL East Mall shoppers. They already collect vouchers in the mall's app, but nothing in it helps them park.

Customer: SDP's malls

Starting with KL East Mall

  • Need: a reason to choose their mall when parking is tight, and to keep shoppers coming back
  • Without: hardware on every bay, or bays lost to unused reservations

The mall's best customers

Regular, high-spending shoppers

  • Need: a reward they feel every visit, and a reliable bay at peak
  • Today: KL East Mall's app rewards them with shopping vouchers, not parking. 1 Utama's ONECARD shows parking works as a perk

Everyone else

Families, cinema-goers, weekend visitors

  • Need: a bay at a set time: before a film, with a pram, with an older parent
  • Today: they circle, and reserved bays go unenforced

Initial market: KL East Mall first (1,300 bays, sharp cinema peaks, wholly owned by SDP), then KLGCC, Elmina Lakeside and Melawati Malls. Later: other malls with rewards programmes, under licence.

KL East Mall's own app, built for SDP, has a Rewards section with QR shopping vouchers. ParkFlow adds a booking tab and parking vouchers to it; member tiers and points come in phase 2 (A12). App listing last updated Oct 2024; current use to confirm with SDP.

3. Your Solution

ParkFlow: a bookable Priority Zone by the lifts, free for the mall's best customers and shared with walk-ins, plus a forecast for every driver

5:00 pmThe app says B1 and B2 will likely be full by 7:15 pm. Last week's RM300 spend earned the family a free booking voucher, so they book a Priority Zone bay for 7:00.

Priority Zone: the most wanted bays

  • Bookable in the KL East Mall app or by QR; park in any bay in the zone
  • Enforced by one plate camera: non-bookers pay a premium rate while the sign says "booked cars only"
  • Shared: the forecast sets the sign, green or amber, every minute

General parking (~1,200 bays)

  • No booking, nothing changes for 92% of the car park
  • Each level forecast 30, 60 and 90 minutes ahead
  • In the app ("B1 likely full by 7:15") and on entrance signs ("B3 has space")

Big spenders (RM300+ in a day)Free: a booking voucher for the next visitThe app's existing QR vouchers, up to 24 hours ahead
Cinema and restaurant customersFree, sponsored by the tenant (RM2)A voucher with the ticket or bill
Care bookingFreeSeniors, OKU companions, prams, pregnancy; by app, phone or at the concierge

Bookings are held until 30 minutes after the booked time; a no-show uses up the fee or voucher. Precedents: Sunway Pyramid bookable bays RM6–8 (2019); 1 Utama ONECARD member parking. Rules: A9; rewards fit: A12.

4. Innovation

A proven idea, made explainable and deployable: hold only the bays booked drivers will actually use, share the rest, and make it a member perk

Existing approachMain limitation
Member parking areas (1 Utama ONECARD Preferred Parking)A fixed area: held even when members aren't coming, and no bay is guaranteed
Reserved bays for VIPs, women, families (Mid Valley, Jaya One)Rarely enforced: 34% of UK parent-and-child bays misused
Bay locks; pre-booking apps (SpotHero, JustPark)Hold a fixed share; walk-ins can't use it
Research: learned capacity sharing (Xie et al. 2025; Müller et al. 2026)Works in simulation, but a black box staff can't check
ParkFlowA transparent rule, recalculated every minute, on existing cameras, linked to the mall's rewards

Capacity, not bays

No hardware on any bay: one plate camera and one sign per zone.

Parking becomes a reward

Free booking vouchers for big spenders, in the mall's existing app; member tiers and points next.

Four payers, one zone

Drivers, sponsoring tenants, the mall's rewards budget and licensing malls (A3).

Built on published research. Airline revenue management applied to parking (Teodorović & Lučić 2006). Mixing reserved and walk-in parking raised use by 21% in simulation (Kotb et al. 2016). ParkFlow turns this into a rule a mall can run and audit.

1 Utama: SAYS (2025), ONECARD cardless parking with Preferred and Express Parking areas. Misuse: Confused.com/PCP 2022.

5. How it Works

Counting shows the car park now; one forecast engine shows the next hour, for two decisions

6:30 pmThe Priority Zone is 92% full, but enough cars will leave, so it stays green. B1 and B2 are filling, so entrance signs send other drivers to B3.

A. Priority Zone: green or amber?

At 6:30 pm, 8 bays are free and 15 booked cars are due by 7:00. Is there room for walk-ins?

Counting only: 8 free − 15 booked = not enough → sign amber, walk-ins turned away
With forecast: 8 free + 13 cars leaving by 7:00 − 14 booked cars that will actually come = 7 spare → sign green

The 13 and 14 come from how long each car has stayed, film end times and past show-up rates. Counting can't know either. On a busy Saturday, bays held back while walk-ins wait fall from 12 to 5 bay-hours, with every booking safe (A1). If the forecast fails, the sign falls back to counting.

B. General parking: which level, and when will it fill?

  • Predicts how full each level will be 30, 60 and 90 minutes ahead
  • Inputs: gate and camera counts, GSC show times, bookings, calendar, weather
  • Two models, blended: a pattern model and LightGBM machine learning, with an honest 80% range ("84–90% full")
  • Outputs: the app, entrance signs, and early warning for the mall team
Tested on 30 real car parks: 61% more accurate than "same time last week" (A6).

7. Feasibility

Proven parts on the mall's own cameras and app, for a net cost of about RM36k per mall a year, with fees, sponsors and licences to offset it

Technology: proven

  • Plate-reading entry is live in Malaysian malls (1 Utama, Fahrenheit 88, Bukit Jalil City)
  • Camera bay detection: 97–99% in published studies
  • New part: the zone rule, built and simulated

Resources (pilot zone)

  • 1 plate camera and 1 LED sign at the zone; 2 AI boxes on existing CCTV
  • A booking tab in the KL East Mall app, which already issues QR vouchers
  • Hardware: about RM43k per mall (A4)

Stakeholders

  • Mall management: zone, signs, vouchers
  • Parking operator: gate data, discount at exit
  • SDP digital, IT and DPO: app, security, PDPA

Business model: four payers, one platform

  • Who pays: drivers RM4 a booking; tenants RM2 to sponsor a customer's bay; the mall funds free bookings from its rewards and voucher budget; other malls a RM2,500-a-month licence (A3)
  • SDP's 4 malls: fees and sponsors cover about half the running cost. The net RM142k a year (~RM36k per mall, RM4.90 per booking served) is a loyalty cost (A4)
  • Upside: 6 partner malls a year would make it profitable from year 3; unconfirmed, so not in the base case
  • Market: 173 Klang Valley malls to start; 490 in Malaysia

Deployment

One zone first, run by our team for 8 weeks; then SDP's digital team or a licensed partner. SDP's edge: moving first across four malls, with the data and measured results.

Fees: 20–40 paid bookings × RM4 on 104 weekend days, 5–10 on others, after the operator's 20%. Costs: list prices plus our estimates, replaced with quotes in the mentoring sprint (A4, A14). Not counted: rewards sign-ups, spend uplift, turnover rent. Risks: A11.

What we build next, and why

1

Bookable EV charging bays. Malaysia's EV registrations doubled in 2025 (44,813, +106%) while public chargers grew ~43%. A charging bay is the next bay drivers will compete for.

2

Pay by plate with Touch 'n Go. 300,000+ drivers pay for parking in the eWallet every day. Booking, entry and payment become one flow.

3

Member tiers and points. A meta-analysis of 40 years of loyalty programmes (429 effects) finds they reliably lift repeat behaviour. Parking is a perk felt every visit.

Judging weights from the briefing: impact 25%, feasibility 20%, innovation 20%, commercial 10%, plus strategic fit, team and pitch. EV: JPJ data via NST (Nov 2025); chargers: SoyaCincau (Oct 2025). Touch 'n Go Digital (2023). Belli et al., Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science (2022).

A1. Bookings stay safe with a learned model and day-to-day shocks; if many drivers ignore amber, the zone switches to the simple rule

Busy Saturday, 1,000 Monte Carlo days: bookings that got a bayVIP sectionFixed rule, no safety baysParkFlow
As assumed99.94%100%100%
Stays 20% longer, more show-ups, 10% ignore amber93.4%99.9%99.6%
Stay model learned from a 2-week pilot, 40% cinema-goers99.9%100%100%
Day-level shocks: all stays and show-ups shift together (sd 30%)99.2%100%99.99%
20% of shoppers ignore amber94.7%99.93%99.4%
30% ignore amber92.6%99.7%98.5%
30% ignore + shocks + learned model + cinema-goers87.5%97.8%95.7%
Bays held back while walk-ins waited (bay-h, as assumed)19125
Bays held back in all minutes (bay-h, as assumed)1436233

What it proves

With a model learned from two weeks of data, mis-shaped stays and day-level shocks, ParkFlow keeps 99.99–100% of bookings while holding back a quarter of the bays a VIP section does while walk-ins wait (5 vs 19 bay-hours).

Honest limit, and the fix

When 20% or more ignore amber, the simple rule keeps more bookings (99.7% vs 98.5% at 30%). The plate camera counts amber violations live: above 10%, the zone runs the simple rule until they fall.
Only the pilot can prove: real stays and show-ups at KL East Mall, how many people book, and how shoppers react to an amber sign. Demand levels in these runs are our assumption (A15).

Monte Carlo: each day draws arrivals, stays and show-ups at random from research-based distributions. Learned model: 50 simulated 2-week pilots, each fitting the stay model the rule then uses; show-up rates stay at published priors. Shocks: one random factor a day for all stays and show-ups that the rule cannot see. Script: analysis/simulate_pooling.py.

Honest attribution

Appendix

A5. How big should the Priority Zone be? About 6–10% of the car park, with 20–30% of it bookable at once

Recommended

6–10% of the car park (78–130 bays in a 1,300-bay mall), bookings capped at 20–30% of the zone. Our 100-bay pilot sits inside this band.

Smaller or bigger?

Below 6%, the zone turns away 11–77% of busy-day requests, though every booking it takes still gets a bay. Above ~12%, little improves.

One block or across levels

Pieces on several levels run as one pool work like one block. Run as 4 separate pieces, bays held empty rise ~60%.

1,000 Monte Carlo days per setting: 9 zone sizes × 3 caps × busy, normal and stress days. Choice rule set before running: the smallest zone that keeps ≥99.5% of bookings on a stress day and accepts ≥90% of busy-day requests. Script: analysis/simulate_zone_size.py.

The blend beats either model alone by 5–10%. Most of the gain over "last week" comes from the pattern model itself.

The day shown is typical (median error). Departures and show-ups use the same engine and are calibrated on KL East Mall's data in pilot weeks 1–2. Script: analysis/backtest_ensemble.py.

Appendix

A7. Forecast engine: two models, blended, with an honest range

Inputs

Gate and plate-camera times
CCTV bay counts
Bookings × show-up history
Calendar, GSC shows, weather
❯

Two models

Pattern model
What this hour usually looks like, adjusted to today
LightGBM
Gradient-boosted trees: how events, weather and bookings change it
❯

Blend

Stacked ensemble
Weights re-learned each week from each model's recent errors
❯

Range

Conformal prediction
Past errors become an honest 80% range
❯

Output

Zone rule: cautious departures and show-ups
Mall team: fan chart and top reasons

Industry standard. Combining models is the main lesson of the M4 forecasting competition: 12 of the 17 most accurate methods were combinations. LightGBM was used by most top teams in M5. Conformal prediction is the standard way to make forecast ranges honest.

Runs itself, fails safe

Retrains every night and tracks its own error. If a data feed breaks or bookings start missing bays, the zone falls back to the fixed rule.

Roadmap. Pilot: this ensemble. After 6–12 months of mall data: test a Temporal Fusion Transformer as a third member, kept only if it beats the ensemble. Later: one shared model across SDP's four malls.

Appendix

A9. Booking rules: free for big spenders and for those who need it most, RM4 for anyone else, and rules that stop "just in case" bookings

RuleAnyoneVoucher (big spender or tenant-sponsored)Phase 2: Gold member
PriceRM4 guarantee feeFreeFree
Care bookingFree for anyone: seniors 60+, OKU companions, prams, pregnancy. By app, phone or at the concierge
Book aheadUp to 2 hours, or by QR at the zoneUp to 24 hoursUp to 24 hours
Bookings at onceOne per plateOne per voucherOne per account
CancelRefund up to 30 min beforeVoucher back up to 30 min beforeFree up to 30 min before
Held until30 minutes after the booked time (15-minute window + 15 minutes grace), then released
No-showFee keptVoucher used upCounts against free bookings

Why charge at all?

Free bookings get made "just in case": 9–13% of free restaurant bookings are no-shows (Tse & Poon 2016). So we expect ~80% of free and ~95% of paid bookings to turn up.

Why vouchers

KL East Mall's app already runs QR vouchers. A no-show uses the voucher up, which discourages "just in case" bookings. We still model vouchers at the cautious free show-up rate (80%).

No booking: green = park as usual · amber = go to the level shown, book by QR if there's room, or park and pay the premium rate · red = full. A car that entered on green pays the normal rate even if the sign turns amber later. OKU bays stay outside the zone.

RM300 threshold and the Gold tier are examples for the mall to set. Precedents: Sunway Pyramid bookable bays RM6–8, held 1 hour (Autobuzz 2019); ParkEasy KL ~RM3–4 (Vulcan Post 2015).

A11. The main risks are access and adoption, not technology, and each has a plan

RiskHow we handle it
Drivers ignore amber, or a booked driver finds the zone fullThe camera counts amber violations live; above 10% the zone runs the simple rule. A booked driver without a bay gets the nearest free bay, a refund and free parking; the concierge is alerted.
Free (voucher) bookings made "just in case"One booking per voucher; a no-show uses it up; release 30 minutes after the booked time. The forecast learns show-up rates.
KL East's app has vouchers but no member tiersLaunch with vouchers in the existing app; add tiers and points in phase 2. Partner malls plug in their own programme.
Non-bookers feel shut outAmber only when needed; the sign always says where free bays are; anyone can book for RM4. OKU bays are never held.
Parking system can't discount by plateGive a voucher or points for the next visit instead.
Parking operator is slow to share gate dataSDP asks for it under the operator contract. Fallback: our own zone and floor-entrance cameras.
Privacy concernsCameras never identify cars. Non-member plates scrambled daily and deleted after 24 hours. PDPA notices at entrances.

Appendix

A13. Barrier or no barrier? A plate camera and a sign hold the zone without a queue inside the car park

OptionHow it worksStrengthWeaknessVerdict
Plate camera and sign, no barrierLogs every plate entering the zone. Non-bookers who park there while the sign is amber pay a posted premium rate at exit.No queue inside, no change to fire exits, low costSome ignore the sign: 10% still leaves 99.9% of bookings with a bay; above 10%, the simple rule takes over (A1)Main
Barrier at zone entranceOpens only for booked plates while the zone is heldStrictQueue inside the car park; changes exit routes, so needs Bomba approvalLater, if needed
UHF RFID windscreen tagFree sticker for regular bookers (EPC Gen2). Backup when a plate can't be read.Malaysians know RFID from tollsMetallic window tint can block itTest first
Lock or bollard on each bayApp unlocks a single bayVery preciseCostly, upkeep per bay, still empty until arrivalNo

Zone layout

Placed behind one aisle entry. A car still inside after 10 minutes is parked; one that leaves sooner drove through.

Fair warning and disputes

The premium rate is posted before entry. Disputes go to the concierge with the camera log; first-time and care-eligible drivers are waived.

Fallback

If the plate camera fails, the zone opens to all. If the operator can't bill by plate, the discount becomes a voucher.

Appendix

A16. Why not buy from a vendor, and couldn't others copy it? Buy the hardware, own the rule and the data

OptionWhat it givesWhat it misses
Upgrade the vendor's guidance system (e.g. Hikvision)Accurate free-bay counts, per bayNo booking, no rewards link, no forecast. The vendor holds the data.
A generic pre-booking appQuick to launchSells a fixed share of bays. Another app, not linked to the mall's rewards or gates.
ParkFlowShared zone, forecast rule, rewards perks, inside the mall's own appNeeds a small team to run it

Couldn't another mall build its own?

Yes: the parts are commodities, and we don't claim a technology moat. SDP's edge is moving first across four malls: data from many car parks improves the forecast, and measured pilot results a newcomer won't have.

Licensing is upside, not the plan

ParkFlow works with any rewards programme, so it can later serve malls that already run one, such as 1 Utama or IOI. For SDP's own malls it is a loyalty cost of about RM36k per mall a year (A4).
